# Kupava – Ukrainian folk ensemble and choir from Brno (Czech Republic)

> Kupava (Купава; Ukrajinský folklorní soubor KUPAVA, z.s.) is a Ukrainian folk ensemble and choir based in Brno, Czech Republic, founded in February 2023. It performs traditional Ukrainian polyphonic singing – folk songs from many regions of Ukraine, Christmas carols (koliadky) and New Year songs (shchedrivky) – in traditional dress and with live music. Artistic director: Kateryna Mykhaylova. Website in Czech, Ukrainian and English.

## Key facts
- Type: Ukrainian folk ensemble / folk choir (Czech: ukrajinský folklorní soubor, pěvecký sbor; Ukrainian: український фольклорний ансамбль, хор)
- Based in: Brno, Czech Republic (registered office Rajhrad), non-profit association, Reg. no. 23686766
- Founded: February 2023, with the support of the Ukrainian Centre in Brno
- Performances: 46 since 2023 in Czechia, Slovakia and Austria, incl. the Strážnice International Folklore Festival, Smetana’s Litomyšl, the Chod Festival, Jánošík’s Ducat and a live TV Noe broadcast (Concert for Life II, 2025)
- Programmes: Old Ukrainian Christmas (carols and shchedrivky with the Christmas star); Songs of Ukraine’s Regions
- Contact: kupava@kupavabrno.cz, +420 777 072 433

## FAQ
### What is Kupava?
Kupava is a Ukrainian folk ensemble and choir from Brno, Czech Republic, founded in February 2023. It performs Ukrainian folk songs and Christmas carols in traditional polyphony, in traditional dress and with live music. Artistic director: Kateryna Mykhaylova.

### Is there a Ukrainian choir in Brno?
Yes. Kupava is a Ukrainian folk ensemble and choir based in Brno that performs across the Czech Republic and abroad. It brings together Ukrainian women living in Czechia and Czechs who love Ukrainian folklore.

### What Ukrainian songs does Kupava sing?
Lyrical, ritual and dance folk songs from many regions of Ukraine, as well as Christmas carols (koliadky) and New Year songs (shchedrivky) – always in Ukrainian and in traditional polyphony, e.g. Zeleneie zhyto, zelene or Dobryi vechir tobi, pane hospodariu.

### Is Kupava a folk ensemble or a choir?
Both. As a choir, Kupava sings in polyphony – choral singing is the heart of every performance. As a folk ensemble, it presents folk songs in traditional costume with live folk music: violin, accordion, double bass, bandura and cimbalom.

### What is polyphonic singing?
Polyphonic singing means a song is sung in several voices at once. In Ukrainian folk tradition the lower voices often carry the melody while a high upper voice – the pidholosok – soars above them. This is how Kupava sings folk songs and carols.

### Does Kupava perform at Advent and Christmas concerts?
Yes. During Advent the ensemble presents its programme Old Ukrainian Christmas with carols and shchedrivky – in recent years at St Joseph’s Church in Brno, by the Jošt statue on Moravské náměstí, at the Palace of Noblewomen and in Vienna.

### Where can I hear Kupava live?
At folklore festivals (e.g. the Strážnice International Folklore Festival, Smetana’s Litomyšl, the Chod Festival) and at concerts and Christmas programmes in Brno and Vienna. Next performance: Old Ukrainian Christmas at Jošt, 5 December 2026 (Moravské náměstí, Brno). Recordings are on YouTube.

### How is Ukrainian Christmas celebrated?
Since 2023 most Ukrainians celebrate Christmas on 25 December. On Christmas Eve families gather for a meal of twelve meatless dishes, and carol singers go from house to house with an eight-pointed star. On Shchedryi Vechir, New Year’s Eve, people sing shchedrivky. Every year Kupava presents its programme Old Ukrainian Christmas.

### What are koliadky and shchedrivky?
Koliadky are Christmas carols sung from Christmas Eve onwards. Shchedrivky are New Year songs wishing abundance and happiness to the household. The world’s best-known shchedrivka is Shchedryk by Mykola Leontovych – known in English as Carol of the Bells.

### What does Ukrainian traditional dress look like?
Its heart is the embroidered shirt, the vyshyvanka, with ornaments typical of each region. Women wear it with a skirt or wrap-around plakhta, a vest, coral necklaces and a flower wreath with ribbons (vinok) or a headscarf. Kupava’s singers perform in traditional dress from different regions of Ukraine.

### How can I contact the ensemble?
For performances or joint projects, write to kupava@kupavabrno.cz, call +420 777 072 433 or use the contact form on this website.
